title: Aligos Therapeutics Announces the Completion of Enrollment in the Phase 2 B-SUPREME Study of Pevifoscorvir Sodium Under Development for the Treatment of Chronic HBV Infection

analysis.time: Publication date: July 13, 2026. Event date: Enrollment completion occurred on July 13, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Global study sites worldwide. Approximately 250 untreated HBeAg+ and HBeAg- adult subjects with chronic HBV infection (Part 1a: 131 HBeAg+ participants; Part 2a: 114 HBeAg- participants).
analysis.event: Aligos Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, announced the completion of enrollment in the Phase 2 B-SUPREME study of pevifoscorvir sodium, a candidate under development for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Total enrollment of 245 participants (131 HBeAg+ and 114 HBeAg-). The study is a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled multicenter trial evaluating safety and efficacy. No current cases or deaths are reported as the study is in the enrollment phase. The risk is the ongoing development of a potential best/first-in-class oral small molecule capsid assembly modulator (CAM-E) for chronic HBV infection.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Enrollment is complete. Topline safety and efficacy data are expected in late Q3 2027. The second interim analysis for sample size re-estimation will not be performed due to over-enrollment. The study is ongoing with no unresolved information regarding the event itself, though forward-looking statements indicate risks inherent in drug development.

analysis.brief_en: Aligos Therapeutics announced on July 13, 2026, the completion of enrollment in its global Phase 2 B-SUPREME study of pevifoscorvir sodium, a candidate for chronic hepatitis B virus infection. The study enrolled 245 participants, including 131 HBeAg+ and 114 HBeAg- adults. Topline safety and efficacy data are expected in late Q3 2027. This randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial compares pevifoscorvir sodium to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate over 48 weeks.

title: Study reveals mechanism underlying HBV-induced liver inflammation

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-17. Event date: Not explicitly stated in the supplied evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: Chongqing Medical University (researchers), HBV transgenic mice, liver samples from patients with chronic HBV infection, HBV-replicating hepatocyte cell lines, pAAV/HBV1.2 mouse model.
analysis.event: A study published in Genes & Diseases investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying HBV-induced liver inflammation. The research identified a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent signaling cascade activating the Jak2/Stat3 pathway.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study establishes mitochondrial dysfunction-induced ROS accumulation as a pivotal trigger of HBV-associated hepatic inflammation. It identifies ROS-dependent Jak2/Stat3 activation as a promising therapeutic target for preventing inflammation-driven liver disease progression.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted using in vitro and in vivo models. Pharmacological manipulation of ROS levels (using Mito-TEMPO, NAC) confirmed the mechanism. The source is a news report summarizing a published study.

analysis.brief_en: Researchers from Chongqing Medical University have identified a specific molecular mechanism driving liver inflammation caused by chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. The study, published in Genes & Diseases, reveals that mitochondrial dysfunction leads to the accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which activates the Jak2/Stat3 signaling pathway. This cascade triggers the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and IL-8, ultimately fueling hepatic inflammation. The findings suggest that targeting this ROS-dependent pathway could offer a new therapeutic strategy to prevent the progression of HBV-induced liver disease.

title: WHO, UNICEF question India's newborn hepatitis B vaccine data despite strong overall coverage

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-15. Event date: 2025 (coverage data). WHO-UNICEF WUENIC report released on 2026-07-15.
analysis.location_and_population: Target population: newborns within 24 hours of birth.
analysis.event: WHO and UNICEF questioned India’s official hepatitis B birth-dose coverage estimate (92% reported vs. 70% estimated by agencies) as part of the 2026 WUENIC report. The agencies flagged inconsistencies in coverage denominators and target population calculations. This is a preliminary assessment pending review of India’s NFHS-6 survey results.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: India reported 92% hepatitis B birth-dose coverage in 2025, but WHO-UNICEF estimate suggests only 70% coverage, implying ~30% of newborns missed the vaccine within 24 hours. Chronic hepatitis B risk from mother-to-child transmission remains high for unvaccinated infants. Globally, 13.5 million children were 'zero-dose' in 2025, with 750,000 fewer than in 2024.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO and UNICEF are reviewing India’s NFHS-6 survey results for reconciliation. India’s routine immunisation remains high for other vaccines (e.g., DTP1 at 97%, measles at 98%). The agencies have marked the hepatitis B birth-dose estimate as 'challenged' due to denominator concerns. No official response from India’s health ministry was provided in the report.

analysis.brief_en: On 15 July 2026, WHO and UNICEF released the WUENIC report questioning India’s reported 92% coverage of the hepatitis B birth-dose vaccine in 2025, estimating actual coverage at only 70%. The agencies cited inconsistencies in target population denominators and flagged the discrepancy as ‘challenged.’ While India’s overall childhood immunisation remains strong (e.g., DTP1 at 97%, measles at 98%), the hepatitis B birth-dose gap leaves nearly 30% of newborns unprotected within 24 hours, increasing chronic infection risks. title: Female Newborns More Likely to Miss Vitamin K Prophylaxis, Hepatitis B Birth Dose - The American Journal of Managed Care® (AJMC®)

analysis.time: The study analyzed live births between January 2018 and December 2025 (N5). The AJMC article was published on July 14, 2026 (N32).
analysis.location_and_population: The analysis focused on 93,163 live births at three University of Pennsylvania health system hospitals in Philadelphia (N5). The affected population included newborn infants, specifically comparing male and female newborns (N1, N8, N12).
analysis.event: A retrospective cohort study investigated whether newborn sex influences parental decisions regarding vitamin K (VK) prophylaxis and hepatitis B (HBV) vaccine administration at birth (N5). The findings indicated that female newborns were more than twice as likely as boys to have their parents decline VK prophylaxis (N1, N8).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among the cohort, 777 infants (8.3 per 1000 births) did not receive VK prophylaxis, and 9400 (100.9 per 1000 births) did not receive the HBV birth dose (N6). VK decline rates among female newborns rose from 9.6 per 1000 births in 2018 to 19.8 per 1000 in 2025 (N11). By 2025, nearly 1 in 6 newborns did not receive the HBV birth dose (N14). The risk of life-threatening VKDB (vitamin K deficiency bleeding) increases for infants who do not receive VK prophylaxis (N2, N4).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted within a single health system, potentially limiting generalizability (N25). The authors were unable to assess subsequent clinical outcomes, such as VKDB or neonatal hepatitis B infection, beyond the birth hospitalization (N26). analysis.brief_en: A retrospective cohort study of 93,163 live births in Philadelphia found that female newborns were more than twice as likely as boys to have their parents decline vitamin K prophylaxis, with rates rising from 9.6 to 19.8 per 1,000 births between 2018 and 2025. While the hepatitis B birth dose gap was smaller, nearly 1 in 6 newborns did not receive it by 2025. The researchers attribute the VK disparity to circumcision incentives for boys and note that a CDC policy shift allowing shared clinical decision-making for HBV may be contributing to declining uptake. The study has limitations regarding generalizability and inability to assess long-term clinical outcomes.

analysis.time: The article was published on July 15, 2026, reporting on an initiative announced by the Health Bureau (SSM) on Tuesday, with World Hepatitis Day on July 28, 2026, as a central focus.
analysis.location_and_population: The initiative targets residents aged 50 and above, with screening thresholds lowered to 40 years old since June 2026. It also addresses the general adult population and aims to reach over 19,000 people aged 50 and above by the end of 2025.
analysis.event: The Health Bureau (SSM) announced an expanded push to curb hepatitis B infections, including broader screening, expanded treatment access, and community outreach. This is an official public health initiative.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Health officials estimate that 7 to 8 out of every 100 residents may be infected. The hepatitis B surface antigen positivity rate in the adult population is 7.6% (based on a 2016 survey). Liver cancer accounts for 10.5% of cancer deaths in Macau. The initiative aims to identify silent infections earlier and reduce progression to severe liver disease.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Authorities have implemented automatic hepatitis B testing for residents aged 50 and above with no prior record since February 2025, lowering the threshold to 40 years old since June 2026. All nine public health centers launched dedicated liver clinics in December 2024, with 2,866 visits recorded as of June. Updated survey results are expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Community events, including a "Healthy Community Pop-up Station" on July 18 and a World Hepatitis Day event on July 25 offering free anonymous rapid testing, are planned.

Officials estimate that 7 to 8 out of every 100 residents may be infected, with a surface antigen positivity rate of 7.6% in the adult population. Screening is now automatic for residents aged 50 and above (lowered to 40 since June 2026), and all nine public health centers have launched dedicated liver clinics. The initiative aims to identify silent infections earlier and reduce progression to severe liver disease, which accounts for 10.5% of cancer deaths in Macau.
